title: Commitment profile decider and burst-tolerance guidelines for dedicated pools
creator: Marta Ruiz
description: Objective: produce a deterministic decision flow and numeric scoring matrix that maps customer workload signals to a recommended commitment profile for Dedicated (reserved) pools. The output must include default reserved throughput bands, GPU-family recommendations, burst tolerance classifications, preemption/eviction policy defaults, and a lightweight intake questionnaire that SRE/CS can run during sales intake. This ticket will produce the deliverables needed for sales+solutions to give immediate guidance (T-0) and for engineering to create gated automation for provisioning.
notes: Scope excludes contract/legal language; this focuses on operational and technical commitment sizing.
We will align GPU family names to our pricing tiers (e.g., compact, standard, high-memory) rather than vendor model numbers to avoid churn during procurement changes.

Core deliverables: 1) Commitment Decision Flow (document + flowchart), 2) Numeric Risk/Score matrix, 3) Intake questionnaire, 4) Recommended defaults for burst and preemption, 5) Handoff template for SRE to provision pools.

Primary trade-offs: conservative sizing reduces SLA escalations but increases cost to customers; aggressive autoscale/burst reduces initial commit but creates capacity planning complexity for reserved pools.
Intended audience: Solutions Engineering, Sales Engineers, Customer Success, Dedicated infra team, and Platform Reliability.
This design intentionally treats latency-sensitive request streams and synchronous token-generation workloads separately from offline embedding/batch workloads.
We will pilot with two incoming enterprise prospects (FinanceTech Co. and HealthData Inc.) during March to validate scoring thresholds before broader rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Decision flow doc with at least five decision nodes and annotated thresholds is reviewed and approved by Solutions Eng and SRE.
Numeric scoring matrix validated against historical telemetry from 6 representative customers and updated if >15% of pilots fall outside the recommended band.
Intake questionnaire can be completed in <15 minutes by Sales and produces a deterministic 'Commitment Profile' label (e.g., C1, C2, C3).
Provisioning template includes explicit GPU-family mapping, initial reserved throughput range, and burst tolerance flag that SRE can act on without additional PM approval.
Handbook entry created in Confluence and linked in the ticket; internal launch email drafted for Solutions Eng and CS.
Automation backlog ticket created for engineering to accept the Commitment Profile to provisioning API with required fields.
Pilot feedback captured and at least one revision applied before GA date (release: dedicated-2026.04).

intake_questionnaire: Primary workload type: synchronous_text_generation | streaming_chat | batch_embeddings | reranking
Tolerance for degraded output quality during fallback (none | low | medium | high)
Data residency / compliance flags (PII | PHI | regulated-industry | none)
Is persistent KV-cache required across sessions? (yes | no)
Budget guardrails: monthly committed spend floor or target range
Desired commitment duration: 1 month | 3 months | 12 months
Is burst preemption acceptable with notifications? (yes | no | negotiable)
decision_flow_summary: Step 1: Classify workload by latency sensitivity and burst shape (synchronous vs batch).

Step 3: Map score to Commitment Profile: C1 (0-29) = Flexible Reserved (small commit + high burst tolerance), C2 (30-64) = Standard Reserved (medium commit + controlled burst), C3 (65-100) = Premium Reserved (high commit with low burst tolerance).
Step 4: For C2/C3, pick GPU family: prefer 'high-throughput' for embedding-heavy workloads, 'low-latency' for chat (map to vendor H100-like family), 'balanced' for mixed workloads.
Step 5: Output recommended reserved throughput band (tokens/sec) and suggested burst policy (short_burst_minutes, sustained_burst_hours), plus preemption default (soft | hard).
Step 6: If customer requests lower cost, propose model quantization/price-optimized runner as alternative; record as negotiation variant.
Step 7: Generate handoff package with provisioning template and cost estimate for Solutions Eng to present to customer.
Edgecases: If data_sensitivity == regulated-industry -> escalate to Private deployment intake; do not recommend bursty public pools.
scoring_matrix_examples: Example A (Chatbot, high latency sensitivity): latency_criticality=90, peak_ratio=5 (norm->80), data_sensitivity=10 -> score ~ 0.4*90 + 0.3*80 + 0.2*10 = 49; maps to C2 (Standard Reserved) recommending 'low-latency' GPU family and reserved throughput band 800-1500 tokens/sec with short_burst_minutes=10 and sustained_burst_hours=0.5.

Example B (Batch embeddings): latency_criticality=10, peak_ratio=2 (norm->20), data_sensitivity=30 -> score ~ 0.4*10 + 0.3*20 + 0.2*30 = 14; maps to C1 (Flexible Reserved) recommending 'high-throughput' opportunistic models, reserved throughput band 200-600 tokens/sec, burst tolerance short_burst_minutes=60 and sustained_burst_hours=6.
Scoring normalization: peak_ratio_norm computed by capping peak_ratio at 10x and linearly scaling 1->0 to 10->100.
We will refine weights after pilot telemetry; current weights are intentionally conservative on latency_criticality.
handoff_template_fields: Preemption default (soft | hard) and customer notification SLA
Estimated monthly committed spend (USD) and overage billing behavior
Provisioning notes: required KV-cache persistence, pinned model versions, and rollout policy
CS owner and SRE contact for provisioning follow-up
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Under-committing customers who then experience SLA violations -> Mitigation: require a 2-week pilot with telemetry-based re-score and an automatic safety bump to next profile if 99th-pct latency breaches threshold.
Risk: Over-committing reduces capacity for other customers -> Mitigation: implement staggered start windows and explicit capacity accounting; introduce soft-commit trial periods.
Risk: Pricing complexity leads to sales friction -> Mitigation: keep three commitment profiles with clear cost deltas and a simple visualization for Sales.
Risk: Engineering enforcement of burst/preemption defaults delayed -> Mitigation: create automation ticket and manual SRE runbook as fallback; document escalation path.
Risk: GPU family naming drift -> Mitigation: maintain an internal mapping table and a SKU alias layer in the handoff template.
